body.estimand_functional: \(\Theta_{\mathrm{fin}}=\Phi(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{free}})=[\min_{p\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{free}}}\Phi(p),\max_{p\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{free}}}\Phi(p)]\); under the one-unsupported-binary-row assumptions this specializes to \(\Theta=F([0,1])=[L,U]\).

sampling_model.design: Independent repeated complete scenes from prespecified source skeletons; one representative node per supported type--context row is fixed before sampling.
sampling_model.units: Finite source scenes with the relational skeletons in \(Rsrc\).
sampling_model.treatment: The target intervention \(\operatorname{do}(a)\) is fixed; inferential randomness comes from sampled source scenes, not from target intervention assignment.
sampling_model.overlap: Population transfer uses only positive source parent contexts for target-relevant rows other than \(rstar\). For confidence boxes, each prespecified representative source-node parent context is separately required to have positive probability; \(rstar\) remains unrestricted on \([0,1]\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: For prespecified positive-probability representative contexts, construct simultaneous rational coordinate boxes for supported categorical rows, intersect them with row simplices, choose rational \(etahat\), and inflate the center range by the history-adaptive labeled-occurrence radius \(\delta_{\times}=1-\prod_r(1-\epsilon_r)^{m_r}\leq\min\{1,\sum_rm_r\epsilon_r\}\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Definition~3.2 supplies the \(\rho\)-Markovian anchor restrictions: no exogenous relational parent, with a shared non-relational exogenous parent permitted only for attributes of the same instance. Theorem~5.2 and Appendix~D, Corollary~D.7 apply on the intersection with the Section~5 assumptions~(I)--(III), including the global bounded-parent-multiset condition.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The present sharp set is for the fully Markovian no-shared-parent class. Nonconstant values transfer nonidentification only after explicit inclusion in the anchor and Section~5 intersection; sharp ranges and singleton identification do not transfer to a strict superclass.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Canonical finite SCMs reduce arbitrary discrete counterfactual sharp bounds to a polynomial program.
Polynomial programming yields numerical sharp or epsilon-sharp bounds and confidence-region relaxations for discrete causal queries.
Untrusted algebraic root certificates can be checked skeptically by verified univariate CAD and Sturm--Tarski computations.
Root counting and interval subdivision decide univariate polynomial relation systems soundly and completely in PVS.
Exact real-root isolation with multiplicities and nonsquare-free inputs has explicit polynomial bit-complexity bounds.
Unnested univariate parametric Markov-chain model checking is polynomial-time after the parametric model is explicit.
A response-signature LP gives tight causal-order bounds and constructs attaining SCMs.

body.tldr: For any finite family of target-relevant unsupported finite-categorical shared rows, the fully Markovian relational causal set is exactly the compact interval obtained as the image of an explicit rational polynomial over the product of row simplices, with finite-noise endpoint witnesses. The one unsupported binary row remains the tractable specialization with exact algebraic certificates. Here fully Markovian means mutually independent distinct exogenous variables, no exogenous relational parents, and no non-relational exogenous parent shared by distinct ground endogenous variables. Comparison with Ejaz--Bareinboim is only on the intersection of their Definition~3.2 \(\rho\)-Markovian anchor and their Section~5 assumptions~(I)--(III); the global parent-multiset bound is not inferred from the finitely listed groundings. Nonconstant \(F\) transfers nonidentification only when inclusion in that intersection is explicit, and neither the sharp interval nor a singleton transfers to a strict superclass. Supported-row boxes use \(\delta_{\times}=1-\prod_r(1-\epsilon_r)^{m_r}\), while the frozen exhaustive-assignment grammar, rather than relational treewidth itself, accounts for the \(2^k\) incidence witness.

project_justification.gap: Complete relational identification on the published Definition~3.2 and Section~5 intersection does not return the exact compatible causal range after nonidentification. Generic polynomial bounds also do not realize every product-simplex point by a type-shared fully Markovian RSCM or certify the relational derivation and endpoint models.
project_justification.niche: Finitely many unsupported finite-categorical rows admit an exact structural reduction on a fully Markovian no-shared-parent class; the one-binary-row specialization additionally admits efficient exact univariate algebraic certification.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the multivariate structural sharp image and finite-noise endpoint witnesses without a global skeleton-degree assumption, supplies a skeptical univariate certificate, and states published-comparator consequences only on the explicit Definition~3.2 and Section~5 intersection.

body.related_work: Ejaz and Bareinboim's Definition~3.2 gives the \(\rho\)-Markovian anchor: it excludes exogenous relational parents and allows a shared non-relational exogenous parent only for attributes of the same instance. Their Section~5 completeness and neural results apply separately under assumptions~(I)--(III), including finite observed domains and one uniform relational-parent-multiset bound over every skeleton in the declared domain; Appendix~D, Corollary~D.7 is the version-two neural correctness result. The present exact image is proved for a fully Markovian subclass with mutually independent distinct exogenous variables and no shared non-relational exogenous parent, without assuming that global bound. Consequently, comparison is restricted to the intersection with the published Section~5 domain. A nonconstant image proves nonidentification upward only when the fully Markovian compatible class is explicitly included in that intersection; neither its sharp interval nor a constant-polynomial singleton transfers to a strict superclass. Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim provide canonical finite-SCM polynomial programs, and Duarte et al. provide general numerical polynomial bounds and confidence-constraint relaxations; neither supplies this relational product-simplex realization theorem, exact univariate relational certificate, or multiplicative labeled-occurrence enclosure. Li, Passmore, and Paulson, Narkawicz, Mu\~noz, and Dutle, and Tsigaridas and Emiris supply the skeptical algebraic and root-isolation substrate. Hutschenreiter, Baier, and Klein identify a polynomial explicit-univariate model-checking core. Rossetto and Antonucci construct attaining models for order-based nonrelational bounds, but their witnesses do not impose the present type-shared fully Markovian semantics.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Efficient exact optimization and skeptical certification of a general multivariate product-simplex polynomial remain open; the complete exact certificate here is univariate. The frozen certificate transaction also requires exhaustive event-consistent assignment records in \(Ictx\). Even for an edgeless target with \(w=0\), the nontrivial query \(B=\{X_1=X_{k+1}\}\), a fair supported \(X_1\), and unsupported-row \(X_{k+1}\) has \(F=1/2\) and direct relevance but forces \(2^k\) records. This is an obstruction to width-sensitive production for the frozen exhaustive grammar only; a circuit-level incidence grammar and checker remain open. The confidence interval is conservative and is not the exact projection over supported-row boxes.
body.honest_scope: Structural soundness, compact interval form, endpoint attainment, and the finite breakpoint atom-count bound are proved for any finite family of unsupported finite-categorical rows in fully observed, acyclic, type-shared RSCMs with mutually independent distinct exogenous variables, no exogenous relational parents, and no non-relational exogenous parent shared by distinct ground endogenous variables. These structural results do not assume a global bound on relational-parent multiset size. That bound is a comparator-only condition in the Ejaz--Bareinboim Section~5 domain and cannot be inferred from the finite source and target groundings. All procedure and neural-completeness comparisons are restricted to the intersection of that domain with the Definition~3.2 anchor; nonidentification transfers only under explicit class inclusion, and sharp ranges or singleton identification transfer only under class equality. Exact derivative-root optimization, algebraic endpoint comparison, polynomial-size certificates, the sharp optimizer-degree guarantee, and the at-most-two algebraic-noise-mass guarantee remain specific to one unsupported binary row. Efficient exact multivariate optimization, compact circuit-level incidence, conditional postintervention queries, exact nuisance-box projection, and empirical usefulness beyond the documented N3 example remain open. The sampling enclosure is conservative and uses \(\delta_{\times}\leq\min\{1,\sum_r m_r\epsilon_r\}\).
